messages:
katie_support: FYI customer (ACME) reporting a sudden spike of 5xx + streaming timeouts in ap-northeast-1 starting ~09:05 UTC. Multiple clients seeing disconnects and 502/504. Raising for triage.
raj_sre: On it, thanks. Any correlation with deploys or config changes around 09:00?
marc_runtime: I'm seeing a config rollout at 09:01 that changed upstream keepalive from 60s -> 15s on the ap-northeast routing pool (was flagged as a perf experiment). Pushing logs now.
katie_support: Customer says errors began exactly after ~09:05 when their batch jobs started. They sent sample request IDs.
marc_runtime: Log snippet from the edge -> runtime path: ```ts=2025-11-12T09:07:21Z level=error component=ingress msg="upstream timeout" target=runtime-node-12 request_id=acme-req-83 code=504```
raj_sre: Looks like shorter keepalive caused frequent connection churn under bursty traffic; runtime's connection pool couldn't warm fast enough and we hit request queueing + upstream timeouts. Can we rollback the keepalive toggle?
marc_runtime: I agree. The experiment autoscaler also reduced max-conns-per-node -> combined effect. Rolling back keepalive to 60s should reduce churn.
nana: (bot) @channel creating incident WAR_ROOM_APN1_5XX_1753332222
ana: (bot) Paging on-call: raj_sre, marc_runtime
katie_support: I'll notify ACME that we're investigating and ask them to pause heavy fanouts for 20m if possible.
raj_sre: Immediate mitigations: 1) rollback keepalive -> 60s, 2) temporarily increase per-node max-conns, 3) add short-term routing rule to send ACME traffic to eu-west if they agree. I can do 1+2 now.
marc_runtime: Patch ready. Command: ```./infractl deploy-config --region ap-northeast-1 --set upstream.keepalive=60 && ./infractl set pool.max_conns=500```
deploy_bot: rollback job started by raj_sre at 2025-11-12T09:12:03Z
marc_runtime: After rollback, I can also add a guard in runtime to reject or shed new connections when pool warmup < 20% to avoid full queueing. That needs a minor code change but won't be immediate.
raj_sre: Rollback completed at 09:14 UTC per deploy logs. Observability: p50 latency back to baseline, 5xx count dropping. Still monitoring.
katie_support: Customer confirmed error rate is down for initial checks. Great. They're asking for postmortem and action items.
jules_product: Please capture experiment rollout flow + guardrails. We need to prevent experiment toggles that touch keepalive/max-conns without SRE approval.
marc_runtime: Agreed. Immediate action: add a deploy-gate on upstream.keepalive and per-node-conns in the infra repo. Longer term: runtime should have adaptive pool warmup and connection backpressure.
raj_sre: Action items (short): - raj_sre: add deploy-gate and revert policy (due EOD) - marc_runtime: RFC for adaptive pool warmup + guard (due +3d) - ana_custsuccess: draft customer-facing postmortem & SLA note (due 24h) - jules_product: update experiment runbook to include SRE signoff (due 48h)
nana: (bot) Incident notes saved to /incidents/WAR_ROOM_APN1_5XX_1753332222/logs-archive.tar.gz
deploy_bot: rollback completed successfully at 2025-11-12T09:14:12Z :white_check_mark:
katie_support: Thanks team. I'll keep ACME updated and confirm if they want traffic moved to eu-west for the next hour.
raj_sre: Monitoring for 20m. If 5xx count remains steady, we'll close the war room and open a postmortem doc.
marc_runtime: I'll start the RFC and include load test that simulates short keepalive scenarios.
nana: (bot) War room closed for active mitigation at 2025-11-12T09:28:42Z. Follow-ups tracked in the PM doc.
nana: (bot) Summary: root cause = experiment changed upstream.keepalive + reduced max-conns; regression under bursty fanout caused connection churn -> queueing -> upstream timeouts. Mitigation = rollback keepalive, increase per-node conns, optional customer routing; actions assigned.
